title: UNC → ARREST
text: Prior run: nearest facility was on diversion, 11 minutes lost. Route to the second closest.
spoken: Nearest facility was on diversion, eleven minutes lost. Route to the second closest.

title: deferred airway
text: Skipped the supraglottic because family reported recent neck surgery. Compressions continued.
spoken: Prior crew deferred the airway after family reported recent neck surgery.

title: cardiac arrest
text: Adult cardiac arrest: begin high-quality compressions. Advanced airway is deferred when contraindications are present, including known or suspected neck trauma or recent neck surgery.
spoken: Adult cardiac arrest guideline: start compressions. Defer advanced airway if neck surgery is reported.

title: reroute after diversion
text: Committed to the nearest ED that was on diversion. Eleven minutes lost. Outcome: failure.
spoken: A prior run lost eleven minutes committing to a facility already on diversion.

title: UNC → ARREST
text: We found the patient pulseless after a dispatch for unconscious. Compressions started immediately. The first rhythm check showed asystole.
spoken: Prior unconscious dispatch upgraded to arrest. Compressions started on arrival.

title: Airway Management
text: Supraglottic airways are contraindicated in known esophageal disease and should be used with caution after recent neck surgery.
spoken: Supraglottic airways need caution after recent neck surgery.

title: load and go for occult cardiac
text: Dispatched sick, found diaphoretic with a weak radial. We loaded for a cardiac facility rather than the closest house.
spoken: A sick dispatch was treated as occult cardiac and routed to a cardiac facility.

title: forced intubation
text: Attempted intubation despite a reported difficult airway. Two minutes of interrupted compressions. Outcome: failure.
spoken: A prior intubation attempt interrupted compressions for two minutes and failed.

title: Altered Mental Status
text: For unconscious or unresponsive patients, consider cardiac, toxicologic, and neurologic causes in parallel. Do not anchor on the dispatch code.
spoken: Unconscious patients: consider cardiac, toxicologic, and neurologic causes together.

title: SICK → CARD
text: We treated a general-illness dispatch as a cardiac event after the first set of vitals. The patient arrested in the bay.
spoken: A general illness dispatch reclassified to cardiac. The patient arrested in the bay.

title: epinephrine 1 mg IV
text: Gave epinephrine one milligram IV push after confirming the dose out loud.
spoken: Prior crew gave epinephrine one milligram IV after a readback.

title: Toxicology and Overdose
text: Opioid overdose may present as unconscious with pinpoint pupils. Naloxone does not replace airway and ventilation.
spoken: Overdose can look like unconscious. Naloxone does not replace airway support.
